kinds.name: Agate
kinds.look: Drab brown, grey or black outside; often covered with small half-moon chips under 1 cm across; can be pitted.

kinds.name: Almandine garnet
kinds.look: Ball-shaped 12-sided (dodecahedron) or 24-sided (trapezohedron) crystals in schist, gneiss and amphibolite; in gravel, mostly "broken fragments of crystals" (USGS SP14-95, Ruby River).

kinds.name: Aquamarine
kinds.look: Pale blue to blue-green six-sided crystals or grains in pink or white granite: mostly small grains under half an inch, crystals to about 1.3 inches long and 0.3 inch wide (Pattee 1968 p.75), and round knots 2 to 3 inches across that can be 30 percent aquamarine (p.71).

kinds.name: Azurite
kinds.look: Deep blue crusts, little tabular crystals and sprays in cavities of rusty, green-stained copper ore and dump rock; often with malachite.

kinds.name: Beryl
kinds.look: Six-sided prisms, "Green and white crystals ...

kinds.name: Common opal
kinds.look: Glassy to waxy opal without play of colour, in seams, vesicles and cavities: milk white, yellow, brown, red, green or black (RI16 p.9); hyalite is clear and glassy, in botryoidal crusts (GIA 2015).

kinds.name: Corundum
kinds.look: Larger, elongate crystals, "uniformly dull, translucent or opaque, gray-blue to lilac" (Clabaugh 1952 p.55), in gneiss lenses or in placer gravel.

kinds.name: Gem tourmaline (elbaite)
kinds.look: Pink, green or blue prisms in the pockets of the pegmatite, often with smoky quartz; gem varieties "may display different colors within the same crystal" (Dole 1950 p.24).

kinds.name: Galena
kinds.look: Heavy, lead-grey, bright metallic pieces that break into little cubes with square corners; crystals (cubes, cuboctahedra) only in vugs.

kinds.name: Skarn garnet
kinds.look: Brown, green or honey-coloured crystals and massive garnet rock at limestone contacts, often with epidote, pyroxene, calcite and copper stain; the best crystals grew into calcite or open joints and come free "leaving beautifully sharp casts" (Shannon 1926 p.301, Seven Devils).

kinds.name: Jasper
kinds.look: Red, yellow, brown or green; rhyolite-margin jasper is "usually too fractured" (Bonnichsen).

kinds.name: Malachite
kinds.look: Bright to dark green crusts, velvety tufts, radiating needles and banded nodules on rusty copper ore, on dumps and outcrops of copper mines.

kinds.name: Mica
kinds.look: Thick six-sided or ragged "books" of mica, from an inch to a foot across, in coarse quartz-feldspar pegmatite or loose in the soil below it; they peel into thin, clear, flexible sheets.

kinds.name: Native copper
kinds.look: Copper-red to brown or green-coated wires, branching (dendritic) plates, thin films on fractures and small ragged flakes in rusty oxidized ore or dark volcanic rock; often crusted with green malachite or red cuprite.

kinds.name: Native silver
kinds.look: Wires, curls, moss-like and frost-like growths, thin leaves or foil in cavities and cracks of rusty, oxidized vein rock (cerusite, limonite, quartz).

kinds.name: Obsidian
kinds.look: Black to brown glass with a shell-shaped (conchoidal) break and razor edges; float pieces are often frosted or sand-etched (Lange 1965, Ore Bin 27(4)).

kinds.name: Precious opal
kinds.look: Thin layers and nodules in gas cavities, seams and joint fillings in rhyolite (Spencer: vugs "up to six inches", Broughton 1972 p.103); at Opal Butte, inside rhyolite geodes "from a few centimeters to well over a meter in diameter" (Smith 1988 p.230).

kinds.name: Opalized wood
kinds.look: Logs, limbs and flakes with the grain kept, in interbed sand and clay, between basalt pillows and under talus; flakes in the wash at a gully's foot lead up the gully to the bed (RI16 p.21).

kinds.name: Pyrite
kinds.look: Brassy cubes, pyritohedrons (twelve five-sided faces) or octahedra in quartz, calcite or soft sericite; on a dump, in pieces of vein rock and altered granite.

kinds.name: Pyromorphite
kinds.look: Green, yellow or brown six-sided barrel-shaped crystals, crusts and mossy growths in cracks of rusty, limonite-stained vein rock and slate ("The prism faces are usually deeply furrowed horizontally and are frequently curved or bulging giving the crystal a barrel shape", Shannon 1926 p.419).

kinds.name: Quartz crystal
kinds.look: Six-sided prisms with pointed ends, single or in clusters; doubly terminated crystals are rare.

kinds.name: Amethyst (in quartz)
kinds.look: Purple quartz crystals: iron in the quartz turned purple by natural radiation (Fritsch and Rossman 1988); surface amethyst is often pale (Dillhoff and George 2016). Quartz crystal spots with a confirmed amethyst find within 10 km.

kinds.name: Rhodochrosite
kinds.look: Pink to pale pink, often banded or in rhombs; on a dump, in pieces of vein rock with quartz and sulphides.

kinds.name: Rhodonite
kinds.look: Black, heavy, oxide-crusted chunks and boulders; break them and pink shows inside ("When chunks of black oxide are broken, the pink rhodonite usually shows within the specimen", DOGAMI B17 p.21).

kinds.name: Sapphire
kinds.look: Small: mostly equant etched grains or flat hexagonal tablets 2-7 mm across, most well under 1 carat (Berg 2007 B134; Renfro 2018 p.193).

kinds.name: Specular hematite
kinds.look: Steel-grey to black, very shiny flakes, curved plates and rosettes ("broad, lustrous plates, and sheaves", Shannon 1926 p.194), often in quartz, epidote or garnet rock.

kinds.name: Star garnet
kinds.look: Rounded 12-sided (dodecahedron) or 24-sided (trapezohedron) crystals "from sand sized particles to golf balls or larger" (USFS 2026); most are under 2 cm (Evans & Moyle 2006 p.30).

kinds.name: Sunstone
kinds.look: Broken, glassy feldspar fragments with flat cleavage faces, mostly pea to thumb size: the smallest worth keeping "will not pass through a one-quarter inch screen"; pieces to 3 x 1.5 x 1 in (Peterson 1972 p.212).

kinds.name: Thunderegg
kinds.look: A ball from under an inch to 4 feet across, "most are about the size of a baseball", with "a knobby rind of drab, siliceous rock" (Staples 1965); found in the soil and loose rock near its source.

kinds.name: Topaz
kinds.look: Clear, pale yellow or pale blue crystals, short square-ish prisms with a flat end; in the Sawtooth small and glassy in the cavities with smoky quartz and pink feldspar; "colorless, and pale yellow prisms up to 7 mm.

kinds.name: Tourmaline
kinds.look: Black, glossy, striated prisms, often three-sided in cross-section with rounded sides, from needles to fat crystals; "as small and large crystals and as crystal aggregates 6 inches or more across" (Stoll 1950 p.20); "coarse imperfect black crystals" in pegmatite blocks in talus (Shannon 1926 p.341).
